AIRPORT FOLLOWINGs/ SECURITY UPDATE

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
three weeks after our initial story - brazen criminals are still targeting the airport - we speak to Minister Fikile Mbalula

Unique Selling Point:
KEEPING TABS ON IMPORTANT STORIES

Summary:
Three weeks after our initial story there has been one heist, one hijacking and at least three follow home incidents linked to OR Tambo Airport.

After our story security has been upped, tactical teams have been put in place - but when will we see results.

Further information:
NOTES

01 July 2107 – SATURDAY
OR TAMBO INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT CARGO HEIST
- a group of approximately eight suspects, some of whom were wearing security company reflector jackets, entered the cargo terminal in two cars.
- Some suspects took control of the main gate, while the others proceeded to a Swiss-port warehouse and stole a truck carrying cellphones.
- Two suspects fled on foot across the R21 highway.
- One of them was killed in a shoot-out with a Gauteng K9 member while the second was arrested. Firearms recovered.
- Another section of the group fled in the hijacked truck, which was later abandoned on the R24 before the suspects fled on foot.
- A third group of suspects fled in a sedan, which they had hijacked from one of the airport security personnel. The abandoned vehicle was later recovered in Alexandra.
-
08 July 2107 – SATURDAY
OR TAMBO INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT FOLLOW HOME
- A couple returning from a trip and landing at OR Tambo International Airport over the weekend have been robbed of luggage worth and estimated "R50 000 and some $7 000 in cash".
- The alleged 'follow-home' robbery took place in Centurion on Saturday night 8 July, after the couple left the Johannesburg airport.
- The report quotes police spokesperson Captain Dave Miller, who states the robbery occurred on the "corner of Rietvlei Dam Street and Delmas Road", after "five armed men in a silver Mercedes forced the couple to stop".
- Miller says the couple was not injured, but their cellphones were also stolen during the robbery.
- Attempts to track the robbers via the cellphones by security forces responding to the situation "lead to Hammnaskraal" but the signal was eventually lost.

10 July 2107 – MONDAY
OR TAMBO INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT TRUCK HIJACKING
- A truck carrying precious cargo was hijacked ahead of Police Minister Fikile Mbalula’s visit to OR Tambo International Airport on Monday morning.
- The truck was hijacked outside a gate at the airport called "Super South" after having left an area where goods such as currency are kept, the airport's general manager Bongiwe Pityi told reporters during Mbalula's visit.
- Airport officials, police, and Ekurhuleni metro police found the truck abandoned, and the hijackers had fled.
- Although it was not immediately clear what was in the truck, Pityi said they were certain it was carrying high-value goods.

Press Release:


Airport Heists Follow Up
Three weeks ago Carte Blanche revealed how alleged spotters work within the airport to identify travellers with high value goods before following them and robbing them
on their way home. Since then there have been three so-called follow-home robberies, one hijacking and one truck heist linked to the OR Tambo airport. Police minister
Fikile Mbalula has assured the public that security measures have been sharpened and tactical teams put in place. But when will we see actual results?

Script:


STRUCTURE FOLLOW UP

VO: Crime has beset travellers at the OR Tambo International Airport with a spate of airport following robberies.

At the time of our last story, there had been 19 confirmed incidents since January - three travellers were shot and wounded. No arrests were made.

NEW LINK: Since our story, there has been five so-called follow-home robberies, one hijacking and one truck heist linked to the OR Tambo airport within the space of just three weeks – it’s not getting any better.

VO: Police Minister Fikile Mbalula addressed the media at a briefing held at the airport on Monday.

FIKILE UPSOUND: we will have a tough security control that will police everybody in this area – that included all employees at ACSA and everyone working at this airport.

VO: In our last story, we featured an undercover source who claimed to be a spotter. He is employed in the airport and gives robbers information on possible targets – for a fee.

INSIDER: We are placed in different franchises or enterprises // It can be anything from car rentals to securities to porters to cleaners – people that work within // they get details, registrations, check what you’re carrying,// your movements //

VO: Travellers may unwittingly draw robbers’ attention - the clothes they wear, jewellery, luggage sets and even their point of origin – all these are key indicators that can turn a passenger into a prime target.

BASIE: I was disgusted, I wasn’t half an hour in my own country and I got robbed. //

VO: The modus operandi is simple - robbers tail the mark, then they move in when the opportunity arises, they pull weapons on the victims, and make off with thousands of rands in luggage, foreign exchange and jewellery, in a matter of minutes.

On the 26th of JUNE, Angolan citizens left the airport and were robbed as they reached their Hotel in Bruma. The robbers took a laptop, jewellery, watches and about R50 000 in foreign currency.

Later that same day, a Congolese national was followed to a Hotel in Bedfordview, this time, the criminals fired a shot during the hit - again they made off with cash and valuables estimated at R250 000

Then, on the 8th of JULY – a South African couple was robbed on their way home from an international trip. They were hit at an intersection in Centurion – the robbers got away with R130 000 of luggage, cellphones, and electronics.

The very next day, a family from Saudi Arabia were pulled over by what appeared to be police nearing the Cleveland Off-ramp on the M2. While the robbers demanded their luggage, they only got away with around R33 000 in local and foreign currency.

Police Minister Fikile Mbalula spoke to us about their strategies moving forward.

DEVI: Who’s responsibility is the slack security – is it ACSA’s or is the police’s?
MINISTER: It is us – and I take responsibility in terms of the police, it is us – we are blinking there and we cant afford that place that it can be taken over by anybody and the sort of criminality that is going on. It doesn’t mean that criminality will not happen, but the point that criminality happens so fast that it undermines national security // INt1 M10

VO: The tourism industry is extremely concerned about the security threats at OR Tambo – as it is the major gateway into South Africa. Tebogo Umanah if from the Tourism Business Council.

TEBOGO: The issue about the tourism industry is that it is a big contributor to the GDP of any country – contributions to employment – crime will have an impact on the economy - // INT1 M11

VO: According to the World Travel and Tourism Council – in 2016, tourism created over 1.5 million jobs and contributed over R 402 billion (R402.2) to the GDP – that’s 9.3% of South Africa’s GDP. While crimes against tourists are more difficult to quantify, there is no doubt that it will have an impact on South Africa’s international image.

DEVI: The time for playing games is over.
MINISTER: We can’t be sloganizing with the lives of the people and national security and allow criminals to dent our country and do as they wish – they must know as much as they play and they think those firearms are toys – airport is not a place to play. // INT1 M18

VO: Our spotter, told us in June - while the opportunity is there, criminals will continue to take the gap.

BONGANI: Are we ever going to put an end to this or is it just too lucrative?
INSIDER: it’s easy money – // why do you need to work for a month if you can make it in a day.
BONGANI: How much do spotters get paid?
INSIDER: Anything from R200 to R3000 / R4000 Depending on the value of what they are working on – the value of the robbery.

VO: But Minister Mbalula says things are about change.

MINISTER: They’re holiday is over, it’s going to be difficult – we are going to be rough with them. // And it’s not going to be business as usual – and it’s not going to be fire with fire – where we detect them we are going to respond heavily and very rough – INT1 M16

VO: This is not a new trend - airport related crime has been gaining momentum over the last year – something the Minister acknowledges.

MINISTER: I have just been here over two months and this thing has been going on – remember when I touched down I spoke to General Phalane about the airport – and he did nothing about it and I am not gossiping him – I am saying it now – he did nothing INt1 M11

VO: Former acting national police commissioner Lieutenant General Khomotso Phahlane was appointed in October 2015. He was formally suspended in June this year pending an alleged corruption case.

MINISTER: // We’ve got to step up our game in terms of the fight against crime //INT1 M9 //
DEVI: Are we talking tactical teams?
MINISTER We are implementing tactical teams – their response must be faster, //, but we have // to detect crime before it happens and not just be reactive – we must be proactive and those who perpetrated crime if they penetrate our systems we must be able to basically arrest them. INT1 M14

VO: And while the cops are stepping up – so are these brazen criminals. Syndicates seem to be targeting bigger bounties staging audacious heists with heavily armed gangs on airport property.

On the 1st of July - Robbers hit the Swiss-port Warehouse at OR Tambo, stealing a truck carrying cellphones with an estimated value of R10 million. Two suspects fled on foot across the R21 highway – police responded killing one, and arresting the other. The truck and it’s cargo were recovered at another location.

Nine days later a truck said to be carrying high value goods was hijacked outside the "Super South" gate at the airport – the truck was recovered after the hijackers abandoned it and fled – no arrests were made.

MINISTER: We will not respond with broomstick who are heavily armed – for whatever they come with – we are ready for them. // INT1 M17 //

VO: The police had their first pro-active success with airport followings this past Thursday.

A suspicious vehicle was identified during police patrols. The suspects fired at the cops, but after a shootout, the car came to a halt on the R21N outside the airport. Four suspects were arrested and three firearms recovered.

But what about the criminals inside the airport selling information?

The Tourism Safety Initiative offers stakeholders a platform to deal with crime and illegal activities in the tourism sector says Tebogo.

TEBOGO: I think when people are being employed especially at a national key point, the assumption is that people have been security vetted – so maybe yes there has been a loophole that needs to be addressed. INt1 M8

VO: Minister Mbalula plans to shake things up with new blood - Taking the police command structure at the airport, to the next level.

MINISTER: We have intervened and said the airport must be taken over by a major general. INt1 M6 // COMMENT SWAPPED AROUND// we have not employed stooges – we have employed commanders // INT1 M21 END // We need the centre, leadership – you can change people but is there is not leadership there will be security lapses, there must be accountability INT1 M21
DEVI: But when will we see results?
MINISTER: there is short term and long term, the complicated criminality in the airport includes corruption and collusion which will require our intelligence capacity // INT1 M4 // we’ve got no time to waste time. INT 1 M15

VO: It’s the beginning of the end for airport criminal gangs says Minister Mbalula.

MINISTER: I am saying to South Africans – be rest assured for what is happening in the airport and the petty crimes that have been going and terrorising the nation – it’s over. INT1 M16


 
PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Police Minister Fikile Mbalula says the days are numbered for syndicates targeting travellers in airport following attacks.

MINISTER: They’re holiday is over, it’s going to be difficult – we are going to be rough with them. //

PROMO 2
VO: Following a spate of airport robberies, security measures have been sharpened, tactical teams put in place and a planned airport security 'reshuffle'.

MINISTER: // you can change people but is there is not leadership there will be security lapses, there must be accountability INT1 M21

PROMO 3
VO: With airport robberies every week – the threat to the tourism industry is real. Authorities are stepping up and promising action.

MINISTER: We can’t be sloganizing with the lives of the people and national security and allow criminals to dent our country and do as they wish

metadata.Summary: Three weeks after our initial story there has been one heist, one hijacking and at least three follow home incidents linked to OR Tambo Airport. After our story security has been upped, tactical teams have been put in place - but when will we see results.
metadata.Further information: NOTES 01 July 2107 – SATURDAY OR TAMBO INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT CARGO HEIST - a group of approximately eight suspects, some of whom were wearing security company reflector jackets, entered the cargo terminal in two cars. - Some suspects took control of the main gate, while the others proceeded to a Swiss-port warehouse and stole a truck carrying cellphones. - Two suspects fled on foot across the R21 highway. - One of them was killed in a shoot-out with a Gauteng K9 member while the second was arrested. Firearms recovered. - Another section of the group fled in the hijacked truck, which was later abandoned on the R24 before the suspects fled on foot. - A third group of suspects fled in a sedan, which they had hijacked from one of the airport security personnel. The abandoned vehicle was later recovered in Alexandra. - 08 July 2107 – SATURDAY OR TAMBO INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT FOLLOW HOME - A couple returning from a trip and landing at OR Tambo International Airport over the weekend have been robbed of luggage worth and estimated "R50 000 and some $7 000 in cash". - The alleged 'follow-home' robbery took place in Centurion on Saturday night 8 July, after the couple left the Johannesburg airport. - The report quotes police spokesperson Captain Dave Miller, who states the robbery occurred on the "corner of Rietvlei Dam Street and Delmas Road", after "five armed men in a silver Mercedes forced the couple to stop". - Miller says the couple was not injured, but their cellphones were also stolen during the robbery. - Attempts to track the robbers via the cellphones by security forces responding to the situation "lead to Hammnaskraal" but the signal was eventually lost. 10 July 2107 – MONDAY OR TAMBO INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT TRUCK HIJACKING - A truck carrying precious cargo was hijacked ahead of Police Minister Fikile Mbalula’s visit to OR Tambo International Airport on Monday morning. - The truck was hijacked outside a gate at the airport called "Super South" after having left an area where goods such as currency are kept, the airport's general manager Bongiwe Pityi told reporters during Mbalula's visit. - Airport officials, police, and Ekurhuleni metro police found the truck abandoned, and the hijackers had fled. - Although it was not immediately clear what was in the truck, Pityi said they were certain it was carrying high-value goods.
